clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old man presented with progressive dyspnea over 6 months, productive cough, significant weight loss, and respiratory distress. Initial chest radiograph showed bilateral hilar adenopathy and reticular consolidation suggestive of interstitial lung disease. High-resolution CT imaging revealed traction bronchiectasis, honeycombing, nodules, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. A transbronchial biopsy confirmed non-caseating epithelioid granulomas in the alveoli, establishing the diagnosis of pulmonary sarcoidosis. The patient was treated with steroids, resulting in symptomatic improvement.
